title: Integrated sequential catalytic reforming and methanation of biomass pyrolysis vapors for synthetic natural gas production
content: Biomass pyrolysis is a sustainable thermochemical pathway for converting renewable biomass into gaseous, liquid, and solid fuels. The resulting gas, primarily composed of H2, CO, CH4, and CO2, offers significant potential as a renewable fuel; however, its direct utilization is hindered by low energy density and challenges in storage and transportation. To address these limitations, this study proposes an integrated two-stage process that combines biomass pyrolysis with catalytic reforming and subsequent methanation to upgrade biomass-derived gas into a methane-rich fuel, i.e., synthetic natural gas (SNG). Biomass pyrolysis was carried out at 600 °C using 1 g sawdust, followed by catalytic reforming of the generated volatiles at 800 °C using 1 g of catalyst 50(LaNi0.75Fe0.25O3)/50(xCaO–(1 − x)biochar-K), aimed at enhancing the fuel quality of the product gas. Among the investigated compositions, 50(LaNi0.75Fe0.25O3)/50(0.25CaO–0.75biochar-K) exhibited superior performance, achieving the maximum gas yields of 27.65 mmol g−1 H2, 8.81 mmol g−1 CO, 1.39 mmol g−1 CH4, and 7.25 mmol g−1 CO2. Subsequently, the produced gas was subjected to catalytic methanation over a 30 wt% NiO/Al2O3 catalyst using 1 g at 400 °C. This step significantly enhanced methane production, increasing the CH4 yield to 8.71 mmol g−1 while reducing H2, CO, and CO2 concentrations to 4.01, 3.38, and 5.21 mmol g−1, respectively. Furthermore, thermogravimetric kinetic analysis further revealed a lowering of the activation energy from 62.4 to 41.2 kJ mol−1, indicating improved reaction kinetics and catalytic efficiency. The cyclic reusability study demonstrated 96.4% retention of the initial CH4 yield after 8 consecutive cycles. Overall, the integrated pyrolysis-reforming-methanation strategy provides a viable pathway for producing synthetic natural gas (SNG) from biomass, offering a promising route toward sustainable, carbon-neutral decentralized energy systems.
